summary.pack_description:
Collect one of three highlights celebrating signature moments from Chris Chelios' storied career with the Chicago Blackhawks!

This commemorative collection is being released as part of Chelios’ jersey retirement ceremony on February 25, 2024, as the Blackhawks send his No. 7 to the rafters.

Each pack contains 1 mystery highlight that could be either his first goal as a Blackhawk in 1990 (Core #/1,849), breaking the net cam on a goal in the 1995 Western Conference Quarterfinals (Limited #/500), or his game-winning OT goal against the Canucks in Game 3 of the 1995 Western Conference Semifinals (Rare #/250).

release.name: No. 7 Chris Chelios
release.description:
Sale Starts: Sunday, February 25 at 10am CT / 11am ET / 8am PT

 

Price: $7 USD

# Packs Available: 2,599

 

Purchase Limit: Ten (10) pack limit per person for the first 24 hours; limit increased to thirty (30) pack limit per person afterwards. Once the “Buy Now” process has started, users will have 10 minutes to complete checkout before the pack(s) is released for another collector to purchase.

 

Highlights Per Pack: 1

Pack Contents (Highlight Rarity, Edition Size):

  • One (1) highlight with the following probabilities:
    • 71.1% First goal as a Chicago Blackhawk in 1990 (Core #/1,849)
    • 19.2% Breaking the net cam on a shorthanded game-winning goal in the 1995 Western Conference Quarterfinals (Limited #/500)
    • 9.6% Game-winning OT goal against the Canucks in Game 3 of the 1995 Western Conference Semifinals (Rare #/250)

 

Payment Methods Accepted: Most major credit and debit cards. Payments will be made via registered payment processor MoonPay where available; where not available, payments will be processed via Stripe.

 

Fan Marketplace: Packs and highlights are eligible to be sold to other collectors in the NHL Breakaway fan marketplace. See FAQ.

 

Transferability: Packs and highlights can be exchanged in the Trade Lounge™ with other NHL Breakaway users.

 

Blockchain: Polygon

 

Sets Included:

  • Hometown History: Chicago Blackhawks, Series 1 - Preview

 

Collection Guarantee: Series 1 highlights will only be distributed during Series 1, which ends ~September 2024. We will not issue more than the edition limit we have set. Any editions not distributed in packs will not be distributed after the series end date (See FAQ for “Uncirculated Editions”)

 

All sales subject to Terms

details.name: No. 7 Chris Chelios

summary.name: Chris Chelios
summary.description:
Debut to Remember: On October 4, 1990, Chris Chelios made his Blackhawks debut in Chicago Stadium versus the New York Rangers one to remember. In the opening minute of the third period and with two assists in the game already, No. 7 took a pass from Steve Larmer at the point and fired a slap shot past John Vanbiesbrouck to extend the Blackhawks lead to 4-1. Chicago went on to win the game 4-3, with Chelios tallying three points and his first goal with the Blackhawks.

summary.name: Chris Chelios
summary.description:
1995 Western Conference Quarterfinals Netcam-Breaking Goal: On May 11, 1995, in the Western Conference Quarterfinals against Toronto at Maple Leaf Gardens, Chelios scored a shorthanded goal that broke the NHL netcam. In the third period of Game 3, with the Blackhawks up 2-1, No. 7 went blue line to blue line and fired a powerful slapshot past Félix Potvin’s glove and through the NHL’s camera. Chicago would go on to win the game 3-2 and the series in seven games, advancing to the Western Conference Semifinals.

summary.name: Chris Chelios
summary.description:
1995 Western Conference Semifinals OT Winner #1: On May 25, 1995, Chelios closed out Game 3 of the Western Conference Semifinals versus the Vancouver Canucks at Pacific Coliseum. In the first overtime, Bernie Nicholls found Chelios entering the offensive zone where No. 7 faked a slap shot, freezing goaltender Kirk McLean and sliding in a goal that propelled the Hawks to a 3-0 series lead. Chicago would go on to sweep the series and advance to the Western Conference Final versus the rival Detroit Red Wings.
